points.description: States that the bridge table holds a mapping of destination stations (MAC addresses) to outgoing LAN interfaces/ports (a time-stamp may also be mentioned). Explains backward learning: table starts empty, and on receiving a frame (promiscuous mode) with source address Q on LAN L, the bridge adds/updates the entry 'Q reachable via L'. Explains forwarding use: later frames destined to Q are sent only on L (selective forwarding instead of flooding), and gives one benefit (e.g. less unnecessary flooding/duplication, less congestion, better bandwidth use).

rubric.notes: Full mark requires all parts: table contents (MAC to interface mapping), learning from source addresses of incoming frames, use for selective forwarding rather than flooding, and one benefit. Equivalent wording is accepted. Missing parts earn no marks since the total is 1 mark.
